scope.goal: Implement the accepted query-decomposition solution so HistoricalGrossNetParity can select and finish historical strategies in current Gross order without the candidate-loading command exceeding its 10-second timeout, while preserving all approved accounting behavior.
inScope: The HistoricalGrossNetParity candidate-ranking and candidate-page read path that currently times out in LoadHistoricalGrossNetParityCandidateKeysAsync.
A separate current-Gross strategy ranking read using dashboard_strategy_performance_snapshots, which currently covers every Production strategy.
Strategy-scoped candidate reads executed in the existing source order PaperRun, PaperPosition, PaperSettlement, PaperSellFill, LiveOrder, filling at most the configured bounded page size.

Processor/repository state needed to keep one selected strategy active through its Exact and Fallback phases and to advance past strategies proved complete without reintroducing the global candidate UNION query.
Focused unit, source-contract, and PostgreSQL integration tests plus directly affected historical-parity documentation.
outOfScope: Any change to Gross PnL, Gross ROI, Net PnL, Net ROI, Fee formulas, exact-Fee precedence, direct Fixed0p0333 fallback, rounding, historical cutoff, canonical contribution identity, lineage, audit, reconciliation, CAS, or balance application.
Any donor discovery, donor preview, donor matching, or new donor decision.
Any change to ordinary new/post-cutoff Paper or Live accounting, execution, settlement, signal, order, price, size, risk, or trading behavior.
Increasing the configured 10-second command timeout as the fix.
Creating or changing PostgreSQL tables, columns, indexes, migrations, or durable progress records.
Production database mutation, deployment, service restart, configuration mutation, backup, service stop, or trading action during this local implementation task.
scope.periodOrFilter: Candidate discovery remains limited to canonical HistoricalGrossNetParity contributions with proved originating entry strictly before 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z UTC and not already terminally completed for calculation version historical-gross-net-parity-v1.
scope.firstVerification: Inspect the exact candidate SQL, processor state transitions, model contracts, existing indexes, and focused tests; compare the current global and proposed split query plans using read-only Production EXPLAIN without executing the historical candidate query.

requirements.text: Replace the single global ranked five-source candidate query with a separate current-Gross ranking read and strategy-scoped source-specific candidate reads that remain individually bounded by the existing page size and 10-second command timeout.
acceptanceCriteria: The initial candidate read no longer builds one SQL plan that combines ranking all strategies with all five candidate source branches before applying LIMIT.
The ranking read uses the same dashboard snapshot Gross value used by the current implementation when a snapshot exists; Production evidence shows snapshot coverage for 2613 of 2613 strategies.
Candidate reads are scoped to exactly one selected strategy and one source kind at a time, and no individual returned page exceeds HistoricalGrossNetParity.BatchSize.
The configured CommandTimeoutSeconds remains 10 and query timeout protection remains active.

Read-only plan evidence or focused integration evidence demonstrates that the current Production-shaped top-strategy PaperRun read uses the existing strategy/status, fill-order-time, and parity-audit indexes rather than the former global plan.

verification.command: dotnet test tests/PolyCopyTrader.Tests/PolyCopyTrader.Tests.csproj --no-restore --filter "HistoricalParity|HistoricalGrossNetParity" with TEMP/TMP/TMPDIR and results under the marked D:\CodexTemp run
verification.expected: Focused tests pass and prove split strategy/source selection, bounded pages, timeout preservation, and removal of the global candidate-query shape.
verification.evidence: The final focused HistoricalParity/HistoricalGrossNetParity run passed 28 tests, failed 0, and skipped only the four environment-gated PostgreSQL cases. Source-contract coverage proves a distinct ranking read, a strategy selection record passed into candidate pages, five source-specific queries, bounded page size, unchanged command timeout, and absence of the former global candidate-query shape.

requirements.text: Preserve greatest-current-Gross strategy ordering and fully complete the selected strategy before selecting another strategy.
acceptanceCriteria: When no strategy is active, the processor selects the greatest-current-Gross unfinished strategy, using strategy ID as the deterministic tie-breaker already used by the current ranking.
Once selected, a strategy remains active through all Exact pages and all Fallback pages until no candidate remains for that strategy.
No candidate belonging to another strategy appears in a strategy-scoped page.

Strategies proved complete can be advanced past without changing completed audit rows; restart safety continues to derive financial completion from immutable audit evidence rather than an in-memory financial result.
Source traversal remains PaperRun, PaperPosition, PaperSettlement, PaperSellFill, LiveOrder and cursor pagination remains deterministic within each source.

verification.command: Run focused processor and PostgreSQL pagination tests for Gross ordering, one-strategy completion, source ordering, empty/completed strategy advancement, and restart-safe audit exclusion.
verification.expected: All ordering and completion tests pass without a cross-strategy candidate page or skipped eligible source.
verification.evidence: Processor tests prove frozen bounded ranking probes across 50 completed strategies, selection of the 51st without a rank cursor, one-strategy Exact/Fallback completion, current-Gross reload only after completion, and retention of an active strategy through target or Live-balance deferral. A fresh allowlisted loopback PostgreSQL 17 database passed all 4 HistoricalGrossNetParityPostgresIntegrationTests with no skips, including ranking order, three-page strategy-local traversal, source-path preparation, and atomic fixed fallback.

requirements.text: Keep the approved historical financial behavior and ordinary new-bet accounting boundary unchanged while optimizing candidate discovery only.
acceptanceCriteria: The strict originating-entry cutoff remains earlier than 2026-08-10T00:00:00Z UTC and calculation version remains historical-gross-net-parity-v1.
VenueReported, authoritative-Fee repair, complete exact local evidence, and exact historical CLOB calculation retain precedence.

When exact Fee cannot be determined for a financially valid positive-basis historical target, the existing direct Fixed0p0333 decision remains Fee = ROUND_AWAY_FROM_ZERO(B * 0.0333, 8) and Net = Gross - Fee.
No new fallback invokes donor candidate construction, donor preview, donor matching, or donor-selection revalidation.
Existing completed exact, donor, and fixed records remain excluded and unchanged; ordinary new/post-cutoff Paper and Live Fee/Net paths are untouched.

verification.command: Run the existing direct Fixed0p0333, exact-precedence, cutoff, completed-row, legacy compatibility, VenueReported revision, and ordinary PolymarketFeeAccountingService tests.
verification.expected: All existing financial and historical-boundary tests pass without expectation changes unrelated to candidate-query decomposition.
verification.evidence: The final financial regression matrix passed 102 tests, failed 0, and skipped only the same four environment-gated PostgreSQL cases; the dedicated PostgreSQL run then passed those 4/4 with no skips. Coverage includes strict cutoff, completed-row exclusion, exact-before-fixed precedence, direct Fixed0p0333 rounding, no new donor dispatch, PolymarketFeeAccountingService, and VenueReportedRevision behavior.

requirements.text: Deliver the query decomposition as a local C#/.NET change with bounded verification and no database schema or Production operation.
acceptanceCriteria: No PostgreSQL schema object, migration, configuration timeout, deployment artifact, or Production data is changed by this implementation task.
Logs or structured evidence identify selected strategy and source-specific candidate-read progress sufficiently to diagnose any remaining timeout.
Focused tests, affected solution build, git diff checks, requirement validators, and an independent semantic review pass before completion.
The final handoff explicitly states that the user must deploy the resulting service before runtime Production behavior can be verified.
